chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: If you feed a large language model the phrase,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Michael Jordan plays the sport of blank,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and you have it predict what comes next,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and it correctly predicts basketball,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: this would suggest that somewhere,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: inside its hundreds of billions of parameters,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: it's baked in knowledge about a specific person

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and his specific sport.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And I think in general,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: anyone who's played around with one of these models

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: has the clear sense that it's memorized

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: tons and tons of facts.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: So a reasonable question you could ask is,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: how exactly does that work?

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And where do those facts live?

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Last December, a few researchers from Google DeepMind

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: posted about work on this question,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and they were using the specific example

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: of matching athletes to their sports.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And although a full mechanistic understanding

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: of how facts are stored remains unsolved,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: they had some interesting partial results,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: including the very general high-level conclusion

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that the facts seem to live

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: inside a specific part of these networks,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: known fancifully as the multilayer perceptrons,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: or MLPs for short.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In the last couple of chapters,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: you and I have been digging into the details

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: behind transformers,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: the architecture underlying large language models,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and also underlying a lot of other modern AI.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In the most recent chapter,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: we were focusing on a piece called attention.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And the next step for you and me

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is to dig into the details of what happens

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: inside these multilayer perceptrons,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: which make up the other big portion of the network.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: The computation here is actually relatively simple,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: especially when you compare it to attention.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: It boils down essentially to a pair of matrix multiplications

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: with a simple something in between.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: However, interpreting what these computations are doing

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is exceedingly challenging.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Our main goal here is to step through the computations

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and make them memorable,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: but I'd like to do it in the context of showing

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: a specific example of how one of these blocks could,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: at least in principle, store a concrete fact.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Specifically, it'll be storing the fact

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that Michael Jordan plays basketball.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: I should mention the layout here is inspired

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: by a conversation I had with one of those

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: deep mind researchers, Neil Nanda.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: For the most part, I will assume that you've either

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: watched the last two chapters,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: or otherwise you have a basic sense

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: for what a transformer is,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: but refreshers never hurt,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: so here's the quick reminder of the overall flow.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: You and I have been studying a model

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that's trained to take in a piece of text

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and predict what comes next.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: That input text is first broken into a bunch of tokens,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: which means little chunks that are typically words

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: or little pieces of words,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and each token is associated with a high-dimensional vector,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: which is to say a long list of numbers.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: This sequence of vectors then repeatedly passes through

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: two kinds of operation.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Attention, which allows the vectors to pass information

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: between one another,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and then the multilayered perceptrons,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: the thing that we're going to dig into today.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And also there's a certain normalization step in between.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: After the sequence of vectors has flowed through

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: many, many different iterations of both of these blocks,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: by the end, the hope is that each vector

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: has soaked up enough information,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: both from the context,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: all of the other words in the input,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and also from the general knowledge

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that was baked into the model weights through training,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that it can be used to make a prediction

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: of what token comes next.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: One of the key ideas that I want you to have in your mind

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is that all of these vectors live in a very, very high-dimensional space,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and when you think about that space,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: different directions can encode different kinds of meaning.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: So a very classic example that I like to refer back to

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is how if you look at the embedding of woman

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and subtract the embedding of man,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and you take that little step

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and you add it to another masculine noun,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: something like uncle,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: you land somewhere very, very close

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: to the corresponding feminine noun.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In this sense,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: this particular direction encodes gender information.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: The idea is that many other distinct directions

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: in this super high-dimensional space

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: could correspond to other features

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that the model might want to represent.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In a transformer,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: these vectors don't merely encode the meaning of a single word, though.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: As they flow through the network,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: they imbibe a much richer meaning

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: based on all the context around them,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and also based on the model's knowledge.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Ultimately, each one needs to encode

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: something far, far beyond the meaning of a single word,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: since it needs to be sufficient to predict what will come next.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: We've already seen how attention blocks let you incorporate context,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: but a majority of the model parameters

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: actually live inside the MLP blocks,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and one thought for what they might be doing

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is that they offer extra capacity to store facts.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Like I said,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: the lesson here is going to center on the concrete toy example

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: of how exactly it could store the fact

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that Michael Jordan plays basketball.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Now this toy example is going to require

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that you and I make a couple of assumptions

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: about that high-dimensional space.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: First, we'll suppose that one of the directions

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: represents the idea of a first name Michael,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and then another, nearly perpendicular direction,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: represents the idea of the last name Jordan,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and then yet a third direction

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: will represent the idea of basketball.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: So specifically what I mean by this

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is if you look in the network

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and you pluck out one of the vectors being processed,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: if its dot product with this first name Michael direction is 1,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that's what it would mean for the vector

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: to be encoding the idea of a person with that first name.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Otherwise, that dot product would be 0 or negative,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: meaning the vector doesn't really align with that direction.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And for simplicity,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: let's completely ignore the very reasonable question

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: of what it might mean if that dot product was bigger than 1.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Similarly, its dot product with these other directions

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: would tell you whether it represents the last name Jordan.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Or basketball.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: So let's say a vector is meant to represent the full name Michael Jordan,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: then its dot product with both of these directions would have to be 1.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Since the text Michael Jordan spans two different tokens,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: this would also mean we have to assume that an earlier attention block

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: has successfully passed information to the second of these two vectors

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: so as to ensure that it can encode both names.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: With all of those as the assumptions,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: let's now dive into the meat of the lesson.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: What happens inside a multilayer perceptron?

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: You might think of this sequence of vectors flowing into the block.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And remember, each vector was originally associated

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: with one of the tokens from the input text.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: What's going to happen is that each individual vector from that sequence

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: goes through a short series of operations,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: we'll unpack them in just a moment,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and at the end we'll get another vector with the same dimension.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: That other vector is going to get added to the original one that flowed in,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and that sum is the result flowing out.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: This sequence of operations is something you apply to every vector in the sequence

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: associated with every token in the input, and it all happens in parallel.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In particular, the vectors don't talk to each other in this step,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: they're all kind of doing their own thing.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And for you and me, that actually makes it a lot simpler,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: because it means if we understand what happens to just one of the vectors

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: through this block, we effectively understand what happens to all of them.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: When I say this block is going to encode the fact that Michael Jordan plays basketball,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: what I mean is that if a vector flows in that encodes first name Michael and last name Jordan,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: then this sequence of computations will produce something that includes that direction basketball,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: which is what will add on to the vector in that position.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: The first step of this process looks like multiplying that vector by a very big matrix,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: no surprises there, this is deep learning.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And this matrix, like all of the other ones we've seen,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is filled with model parameters that are learned from data,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: which you might think of as a bunch of knobs and dials that get tweaked and tuned

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: to determine what the model behavior is.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Now one nice way to think about matrix multiplication is to imagine each row of that

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: matrix as being its own vector, and taking a bunch of dot products between those rows

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and the vector being processed, which I'll label as e for embedding.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: For example, suppose that very first row happened to equal this first name Michael direction

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that we're presuming exists.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: That would mean that the first component in this output, this dot product right here,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: would be 1 if that vector encodes the first name Michael, and 0 or negative otherwise.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Even more fun, take a moment to think about what it would mean if that first row

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: was this first name Michael plus last name Jordan direction.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And for simplicity, let me go ahead and write that down as m plus j.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Then taking a dot product with this embedding e,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: things distribute really nicely so it looks like m.e plus j.e.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And notice how that means the ultimate value would be 2 if the vector encodes the full name

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Michael Jordan, and otherwise it would be 1 or something smaller than 1.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And that's just one row in this matrix.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: You might think of all of the other rows as in parallel asking some other kinds of questions,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: probing at some other sorts of features of the vector being processed.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Very often this step also involves adding another vector to the output,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: which is full of model parameters learned from data.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: This other vector is known as the bias.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: For our example, I want you to imagine that the value of this bias in that very first component

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is negative 1, meaning our final output looks like that relevant dot product, but minus 1.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: You might very reasonably ask why I would want you to assume that the model has learned this,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and in a moment you'll see why it's very clean and nice if we have a value here which is

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: positive if and only if our vector encodes the full name Michael Jordan,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and otherwise it's 0 or negative.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: The total number of rows in this matrix, which is something like the number of questions being

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: asked in the case of GPT-3, whose numbers we've been following, is just under 50,000.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In fact, it's exactly four times the number of dimensions in this embedding space.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: That's a design choice, you could make it more, you could make it less,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: but having a clean multiple tends to be friendly for hardware.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Since this matrix full of weights maps us into a higher dimensional space,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: I'm going to give it the shorthand wup.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: I'll continue labeling the vector we're processing as e,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and let's label this bias vector as bup and put that all back down in the diagram.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: At this point, a problem is that this operation is purely linear,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: but language is a very non-linear process.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: If the entry that we're measuring is high for Michael plus Jordan,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: it would also necessarily be somewhat triggered by Michael plus Phelps,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and also Alexis plus Jordan, despite those being unrelated conceptually.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: What you really want is a simple yes or no for the full name.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: So the next step is to pass this large intermediate vector through a very simple

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: non-linear function. A common choice is one that takes all of the negative values

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and maps them to 0, and leaves all of the positive values unchanged.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And continuing with the deep learning tradition of overly fancy names,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: this very simple function is often called the rectified linear unit, or ReLU for short.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Here's what the graph looks like.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: So taking our imagined example where this first entry of the intermediate vector is 1

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: if and only if the full name is Michael Jordan, and 0 or negative otherwise,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: after you pass it through the ReLU, you end up with a very clean value

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: where all of the 0 and negative values just get clipped to 0.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: So this output would be 1 for the full name Michael Jordan and 0 otherwise.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In other words, it very directly mimics the behavior of an AND gate.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Often, models will use a slightly modified function that's called the JLU,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: which has the same basic shape, it's just a bit smoother,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: but for our purposes it's a little bit cleaner if we only think about the ReLU.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Also, when you hear people refer to the neurons of a transformer,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: they're talking about these values right here.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Whenever you see that common neural network picture with a layer of dots

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and a bunch of lines connecting to the previous layer, which we had earlier in this series,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: that's typically meant to convey this combination of a linear step, a matrix multiplication,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: followed by some simple term-wise nonlinear function like a ReLU.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: You would say that this neuron is active whenever this value is positive,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: and that it's inactive if that value is 0.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: The next step looks very similar to the first one.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: You multiply by a very large matrix, and you add on a certain bias term.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: In this case, the number of dimensions in the output is back down to the size of that embedding

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: space, so I'm going to call this the down-projection matrix.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: This time, instead of thinking of things row by row, it's actually nicer to think of it

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: column by column.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: You see, another way you can hold matrix multiplication in your head

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: is to imagine taking each column of the matrix and multiplying it by the corresponding term

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: in the vector that it's processing, and adding together all of those rescaled columns.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: The reason it's nicer to think about this way is because here, the columns have the

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: same dimension as the embedding space, so we can think of them as directions in that space.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: For instance, we will imagine that the model has learned to make that first column

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: into this basketball direction that we suppose exists.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: What that would mean is that when the relevant neuron in that first position is active,

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: we'll be adding this column to the final result.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: But if that neuron was inactive, if that number was zero, then this would have no effect.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: And it doesn't just have to be basketball, the model could also bake into this column

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: many other features that it wants to associate with something that has the full name Michael

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
chunks.text: Jordan.

chunks.title: How might LLMs store facts
